title: RAW UNREVIEWED: f101r displaced vessel marks a moved participant or a separate depicted object
summary: GDT812's admitted f101r inspection fixes a lower displaced vessel, zero local labels and three complete paragraphs in ten lines, despite two broad visual text bands. Freeze those boundaries and the full text before reading. A proposed whole account treats the displaced vessel as the same participant whose location or state changes across records; a rival treats it as a distinct object within a list or comparison. The decisive obligation is a written relation preserving identity while changing one specified state, with distinct predictions in all three complete paragraphs. The existing image does not independently bind that vessel to any individual word, and the earlier f101r no-label test already failed to resolve meaning. Do not infer one paragraph per visual band or use IDEA322's embryological analogy as a lexical key.

design.mechanism: identity-preserving state transition versus separate-object comparison
design.unit: all three admitted f101r paragraphs and the already viewed displaced vessel
design.contrast: the same vessel participant changes location or state versus another vessel is introduced without identity carry
design.prediction: The transition reading must keep a single participant through all complete records and explain a written state change; the comparison reading must license a second participant and preserve the same complete text. A candidate that can switch identity silently has no selecting force.
design.prior_blockers: GDT812 found no local vessel labels and no independent owner for the displaced object; its no-label trial is closed. IDEA322 already offers a separate developmental-source analogy. Image position alone cannot bind the written participant.
